skills: Interpreting slope and intercept in context

lesson.intro: Two-variable data means every subject in the study carries two numbers, and those pairs are plotted as points in the $xy$-plane. The Digital SAT asks a small, very predictable set of questions about such a picture: which way does it slope, what line or curve fits it, what do the slope and the $y$-intercept of that line \emph{mean} in the words of the problem, what does the model predict, and how far off is the model at a point we actually observed. Almost none of it is heavy computation; nearly all of it is careful reading.

blocks.title: Reading a scatterplot
blocks.body:
A \textbf{scatterplot} plots one point $(x,y)$ for each subject. Describe it with three words.

\textbf{Direction.} If $y$ tends to rise as $x$ rises the association is \emph{positive}; if $y$ tends to fall as $x$ rises it is \emph{negative}; if there is no tendency at all there is \emph{no association}.

\textbf{Form.} If the cloud of points hugs a straight line the form is \emph{linear}. If it bends --- rising slowly and then explosively, or falling fast and then flattening out --- the form is \emph{nonlinear}, and on the SAT the nonlinear choice is almost always \emph{exponential}.

\textbf{Strength.} Tightly packed points mean a strong association; a wide scattered cloud means a weak one. A strong association is still only an association: the SAT never lets you conclude that $x$ \emph{causes} $y$ from a scatterplot alone.

blocks.title: The line of best fit
The model and what each piece means
blocks.body:
For a line of best fit written as
$$\hat{y}=mx+b,$$
\textbf{slope } $m$ = the predicted change in $y$ for each \emph{increase of one unit} in $x$. Its units are (units of $y$) per (unit of $x$).

\textbf{$y$-intercept } $b$ = the predicted value of $y$ when $x=0$. Its units are the units of $y$.

From two points $(x_1,y_1)$ and $(x_2,y_2)$ \emph{on the line},
$$m=\frac{y_2-y_1}{x_2-x_1}.$$
For an exponential model $\hat{y}=a(b)^{x}$: $a$ is the predicted value at $x=0$, and $b$ is the factor $y$ is multiplied by for each unit increase in $x$. If $b=1+r$ the quantity grows by $r$ (as a percent) per unit; if $b=1-r$ it decays by $r$ per unit.

blocks.title: Linear or exponential?
blocks.body:
Look at how the $y$-values change as $x$ goes up by $1$.

\textbf{Constant difference $\Rightarrow$ linear.} $5,\;9,\;13,\;17$ adds $4$ every time, so $y=4x+5$.

\textbf{Constant ratio $\Rightarrow$ exponential.} $5,\;15,\;45,\;135$ multiplies by $3$ every time, so $y=5(3)^{x}$.

In words: ``increases by $\$40$ per year'' is linear; ``increases by $4\%$ per year'' is exponential, because a percent of a growing amount is a growing amount. On a graph, a linear scatter rises at a steady rate, while an exponential scatter is nearly flat and then shoots up (growth), or drops steeply and then levels toward zero (decay).

blocks.title: Residuals
blocks.body:
A \textbf{residual} measures how wrong the model is at one observed point:
$$\text{residual}=\text{actual}-\text{predicted}.$$
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{2pt}
\item Residual \textbf{positive} $\Rightarrow$ the point sits \emph{above} the line $\Rightarrow$ the model \textbf{underpredicts}.
\item Residual \textbf{negative} $\Rightarrow$ the point sits \emph{below} the line $\Rightarrow$ the model \textbf{overpredicts}.
\end{itemize}
Rearranged, $\text{actual}=\text{predicted}+\text{residual}$, which is how you recover a missing data value. If the residuals of a linear fit run positive, then negative, then positive again, the data curve and a nonlinear model would fit better.

blocks.title: The slope and the intercept get swapped
How to attack these questions
blocks.body:
\textbf{1. Label the axes in words before you read the choices.} Write ``$x$ = years since 2000, $y$ = population in thousands.'' Almost every distractor dies immediately.

\textbf{2. For a slope question say the sentence yourself first}: ``for each extra \emph{[one unit of $x$]}, the predicted \emph{[$y$]} changes by \emph{[$m$]} \emph{[units of $y$]}.'' Then find the choice that matches.

\textbf{3. For an intercept question set $x=0$} and ask what that means in the story --- the day the shop opened, the moment the candle was lit, the year $2000$.

\textbf{4. Never extrapolate far.} A model built on $x$ from $1$ to $12$ says nothing reliable at $x=90$; if a choice raises that objection, it is usually the answer.

\textbf{5. Watch the sign convention.} Actual minus predicted --- in that order, always.

blocks.title: Worked example 1 --- slope, intercept, prediction
blocks.body:
A city recorded the number of electric-vehicle charging stations $y$ in the year $x$ years after $2015$. The line of best fit is $\hat{y}=18x+42$.

\textbf{(a) What does $18$ mean?} The slope is the predicted change in $y$ per $1$-unit increase in $x$, and one unit of $x$ is one year. So the number of charging stations is predicted to increase by $18$ per year. (The trap choice says ``increases by $42$ per year.'')

\textbf{(b) What does $42$ mean?} Set $x=0$, which is the year $2015$: the model predicts $42$ charging stations in $2015$. Not ``$42$ stations per year,'' and not ``$18$ stations in $2015$.''

\textbf{(c) Predict the count for $2024$.} $2024$ is $x=9$, so $\hat{y}=18(9)+42=162+42=204$ stations.

\textbf{(d) In which year does the model first predict $300$?} Solve $18x+42=300$: $18x=258$, $x=14.33\ldots$, so during the $15$th year after $2015$, i.e. $2030$. Notice that $2030$ is well past the data, so this prediction deserves a shrug.

blocks.title: Worked example 2 --- residuals and choosing a model
blocks.body:
The table gives a shop's actual weekly sales, in hundreds of dollars, for four weeks; the line of best fit is $\hat{y}=6x+20$.
\begin{center}\footnotesize\begin{tabular}{lcccc}
\toprule
Week $x$ & $1$ & $2$ & $3$ & $4$ \\
\midrule
Actual $y$ & $28$ & $30$ & $36$ & $46$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}\end{center}
\textbf{(a) Residual in week $3$.} Predicted: $6(3)+20=38$. Residual: $36-38=-2$. It is negative, so the point lies below the line and the model \emph{overpredicts} week $3$'s sales by $2$ hundred dollars.

\textbf{(b) Actual sales in a week where the prediction was $50$ and the residual was $+3$.} $\text{actual}=\text{predicted}+\text{residual}=50+3=53$ hundred dollars. If you answer $50$, you answered a question that was not asked.

\textbf{(c) Would an exponential model be better?} The actual values change by $+2,+6,+10$: neither a constant difference nor a constant ratio ($30/28\approx1.07$ but $46/36\approx1.28$). The increases are growing, so the data bend upward and an exponential model is the better of the two candidates --- exactly the reasoning the SAT wants: constant difference means linear, constant ratio means exponential.

problems.stem: The scatterplot shows the number of hours each of $12$ students spent studying for an exam and the score that student earned. Which of the following best describes the association between hours studied and score?
choices: The association is positive and approximately linear.
The association is negative and approximately linear.
The association is positive and exponential, with the score doubling each hour.
There is no association between hours studied and score.
problems.solution: As the hours studied increase, the scores increase, and the points lie close to a straight line. That is a positive, approximately linear association. Nothing in the picture doubles, so it is not exponential.
steps: Follow the points from left to right.
The scores rise as the hours rise, so the association is positive.
The points hug a straight path, so the form is linear.
problems.verify: result = 'The association is positive and approximately linear.'

problems.skill: Reading a line of best fit
problems.stem: The scatterplot shows test scores against hours studied for $8$ students, along with the line of best fit. According to the line of best fit, which of the following is closest to the predicted score of a student who studied for $5$ hours?
problems.solution: A prediction from a line of best fit is read off the line, not off a data point. Go up from $x=5$ until you meet the line; the line has equation $\hat{y}=5x+55$, so $\hat{y}=5(5)+55=80$.
steps: Find $x=5$ on the horizontal axis.
Move up to the line of best fit, not to a plotted point.
Read the height: $5(5)+55=80$.
problems.verify: result = 5*5 + 55

problems.skill: Slope of a line of best fit
problems.stem: A line of best fit passes through the points $(2,11)$ and $(6,27)$. What is the slope of this line of best fit?
problems.solution: Slope is the change in $y$ divided by the change in $x$ between any two points that lie on the line itself. Data points would not do; these two points are on the line.
steps: Compute the rise: $27-11=16$.
Compute the run: $6-2=4$.
problems.verify: result = Rational(27-11, 6-2)

problems.stem: A gym recorded its membership each month after opening. For the scatterplot of $x$, the number of months since the gym opened, and $y$, the number of members, the line of best fit is $\hat{y}=24x+150$. Which of the following is the best interpretation of the slope of this line?
choices: The predicted number of members increases by $24$ each month.
The predicted number of members increases by $150$ each month.
The gym had $24$ members when it opened.
It takes $24$ months for the gym to gain one member.
problems.solution: The slope of $24$ attaches to $x$, and one unit of $x$ is one month, so $24$ is the predicted change in members per month. The number $150$ is the intercept and belongs to the moment the gym opened, not to each month.
steps: Identify the slope: $24$.
One unit of $x$ is one month; $y$ is measured in members.
So each extra month adds a predicted $24$ members.
problems.verify: result = 'The predicted number of members increases by $24$ each month.'

problems.stem: For a scatterplot of $x$, the number of weeks since a seedling was potted, and $y$, the height of the seedling in centimeters, the line of best fit is $\hat{y}=1.8x+4$. Which of the following is the best interpretation of the $y$-intercept of this line?
choices: The predicted height increases by $4$ centimeters each week.
The predicted height of the seedling when it was potted was $1.8$ centimeters.
The seedling reaches a height of $4$ centimeters after $1.8$ weeks.
The predicted height of the seedling when it was potted was $4$ centimeters.
problems.solution: The $y$-intercept is the predicted $y$ when $x=0$, and $x=0$ is the week the seedling was potted. So the model predicts a height of $4$ centimeters at that moment. The $1.8$ is the weekly growth, a different question.
steps: Set $x=0$ in the model: $\hat{y}=4$.
Translate $x=0$ into the story: the moment the seedling was potted.
Attach the units of $y$: centimeters.
problems.verify: result = 'The predicted height of the seedling when it was potted was $4$ centimeters.'

problems.stem: For a group of caf\'es, the line of best fit relating $x$, the number of tables, to $y$, the number of chairs, is $\hat{y}=6x+13$. How many chairs does this model predict for a caf\'e with $12$ tables?
problems.solution: A prediction is a substitution: put the given $x$ into the model and evaluate. The answer is a prediction, not a guarantee about any one caf\'e.
steps: Substitute $x=12$.
Add the intercept: $72+13=85$.
problems.verify: result = 6*12 + 13

problems.stem: The table shows four values of a data set. Which of the following best describes a model for these data?
choices: An exponential model, because the values increase by a constant factor.
A linear model, because the values increase by a constant amount.
A linear model, because the values increase by a constant factor.
An exponential model, because the values increase by a constant amount.
problems.solution: Going from one $y$ to the next multiplies by $2$ each time ($400/200=2$, $800/400=2$, $1600/800=2$), while the differences $200, 400, 800$ are not constant. A constant ratio means exponential.
steps: Check the differences: $200$, $400$, $800$ --- not constant.
Check the ratios: $2$, $2$, $2$ --- constant.
A constant ratio identifies an exponential model.
problems.verify: result = 'An exponential model, because the values increase by a constant factor.'

problems.stem: For a scatterplot of the daily high temperature and the number of gallons of ice cream a shop sells, the line of best fit predicts $58$ gallons on a certain day. The shop actually sold $64$ gallons that day. What is the residual for that day?
problems.solution: A residual is actual minus predicted, in that order. Here $64-58=6$, and the positive sign says the point lies above the line: the model underpredicted that day's sales.
steps: Write residual $=$ actual $-$ predicted.
Substitute: $64-58$.
The residual is $6$ gallons.
problems.verify: result = 64 - 58

problems.stem: A line of best fit predicts that a repair will cost $\$212$, but the repair actually costs $\$197$. Which of the following correctly describes the model at this data point?
choices: The model underpredicts the cost by $\$15$, so the residual is $15$ dollars.
The model overpredicts the cost by $\$15$, so the residual is $15$ dollars.
The model underpredicts the cost by $\$15$, so the residual is $-15$ dollars.
The model overpredicts the cost by $\$15$, so the residual is $-15$ dollars.
problems.solution: Residual $=197-212=-15$. A negative residual means the predicted value was too big, so the model overpredicts, and the data point lies below the line. Sign and wording must agree.
steps: Compute residual $=$ actual $-$ predicted $=197-212=-15$.
A negative residual means the prediction was too high.
So the model overpredicts by $\$15$.
problems.verify: result = 'The model overpredicts the cost by $\\$15$, so the residual is $-15$ dollars.'

problems.stem: For a scatterplot of $x$, the number of years since $2010$, and $y$, the number of landline telephone subscriptions per $100$ households in a county, the line of best fit is $\hat{y}=-3.4x+61$. Which of the following is the best interpretation of the slope of this line?
choices: The predicted number of subscriptions per $100$ households increases by $3.4$ each year.
The predicted number of subscriptions per $100$ households decreases by $61$ each year.
In $2010$ there were $3.4$ subscriptions per $100$ households.
The predicted number of subscriptions per $100$ households decreases by $3.4$ each year.
problems.solution: The slope $-3.4$ is the predicted change in subscriptions per $100$ households for each additional year, and the negative sign makes that change a decrease. The $61$ describes the year $2010$ only.
steps: The slope is $-3.4$.
One unit of $x$ is one year.
A negative slope means the predicted $y$ falls by $3.4$ each year.
problems.verify: result = 'The predicted number of subscriptions per $100$ households decreases by $3.4$ each year.'

problems.stem: The line of best fit for the height of a certain species of tree is $\hat{y}=4.5x+12$, where $x$ is the number of years since the tree was planted and $\hat{y}$ is the predicted height in feet. What height, in feet, does the model predict for a tree $16$ years after planting?
problems.solution: Substituting $x=16$ extends the pattern past most of the data, which is why the value is only a prediction; the arithmetic itself is unchanged.
steps: Add the intercept: $72+12=84$.
The predicted height is $84$ feet.
problems.verify: result = Rational(45,10)*16 + 12

problems.stem: A taxi company plotted $x$, the length of a ride in miles, against $y$, the fare in dollars, and found the line of best fit $\hat{y}=2.4x+3.5$. Which of the following is the best interpretation of the number $3.5$ in this model?
choices: The predicted fare for a ride of $0$ miles is $\$3.50$.
The predicted fare increases by $\$3.50$ for each additional mile.
The predicted fare for a ride of $0$ miles is $\$2.40$.
The predicted length of a ride costing $\$0$ is $3.5$ miles.
problems.solution: The number $3.5$ is added on regardless of distance, so it is the predicted fare at $x=0$ miles --- the flat charge for getting in. The per-mile rate is the slope $2.4$.
steps: The value $3.5$ is the $y$-intercept.
Set $x=0$: a ride of zero miles.
The model predicts a fare of $\$3.50$ for that ride.
problems.verify: result = 'The predicted fare for a ride of $0$ miles is $\\$3.50$.'

problems.stem: The table shows six data points from a study. The line of best fit for these data is $\hat{y}=7x+20$. What is the residual for the data point with $x=5$?
problems.solution: Find what the model says at $x=5$, then subtract that from what actually happened at $x=5$. The residual is positive, so this point sits above the line of best fit.
steps: Predicted value: $7(5)+20=55$.
Actual value from the table at $x=5$: $60$.
Residual $=60-55=5$.

problems.stem: The table shows the value of $P$ at four times $t$. Which of the following describes the type of model that fits the data and the constant that governs it?
choices: Linear, with a constant increase of $40$.
Linear, with a constant increase of $1.5$.
Exponential, with a constant multiplier of $1.5$.
Exponential, with a constant multiplier of $40$.
problems.solution: The differences $40$, $60$, $90$ are not constant, but each value is $1.5$ times the one before it ($120/80=1.5$, $180/120=1.5$, $270/180=1.5$). A constant multiplier is the signature of an exponential model.
steps: Compute the ratios of consecutive values.
Each ratio equals $1.5$.
A constant multiplier means exponential, with multiplier $1.5$.
problems.verify: result = 'Exponential, with a constant multiplier of $1.5$.'

problems.stem: A town's population was modeled by $\hat{P}=1.6t+34$, where $t$ is the number of years since $2000$ and $\hat{P}$ is the predicted population in thousands. Which of the following is the best interpretation of the slope of this model?
choices: The population is predicted to increase by $1.6$ people each year.
The population is predicted to increase by $34000$ people each year.
The population in $2000$ was predicted to be $1600$ people.
The population is predicted to increase by $1600$ people each year.
problems.solution: The slope is $1.6$ thousand people per year. Because $\hat{P}$ is measured in thousands, $1.6$ must be converted: $1.6\times1000=1600$ people per year.
steps: The slope is $1.6$, in units of $\hat{P}$ per year.
$\hat{P}$ is measured in thousands of people.
So the yearly increase is $1.6$ thousand $=1600$ people.
problems.verify: result = 'The population is predicted to increase by $1600$ people each year.'

problems.stem: A reading study produced the line of best fit $\hat{y}=13x+45$, where $x$ is the number of minutes spent reading and $\hat{y}$ is the predicted number of words recalled. According to this model, how many more words are predicted for a student who reads for $18$ minutes than for a student who reads for $11$ minutes?
problems.solution: A difference of two predictions from the same line depends only on the slope: the intercept cancels. Each extra minute adds $13$ words, and there are $7$ extra minutes.
steps: The difference in $x$ is $18-11=7$ minutes.
Each minute adds a predicted $13$ words.
So the difference is $13\times7=91$ words.

problems.stem: A museum uses a line of best fit to predict daily attendance. On one day the model predicted $138$ visitors and the residual for that day was $-24$. How many visitors actually came that day?
problems.solution: Rearranging residual $=$ actual $-$ predicted gives actual $=$ predicted $+$ residual. The residual is negative, so the true attendance must be \emph{below} the prediction.
steps: Start from actual $=$ predicted $+$ residual.
Substitute: $138+(-24)$.
The actual attendance was $114$ visitors.

problems.stem: A tutoring company plotted $x$, the number of practice tests a student completed, against $y$, that student's score improvement in points, and found the line of best fit $\hat{y}=17x+5$. Which of the following is the best interpretation of the slope of this line?
choices: Each additional practice test causes a score improvement of exactly $17$ points.
On average, each additional point of score improvement is associated with $17$ more practice tests.
A student who takes no practice tests is predicted to improve by $17$ points.
On average, each additional practice test is associated with a predicted increase of $17$ points in score improvement.
problems.solution: A line of best fit describes an average, predicted change and an association, never a guaranteed effect and never causation. The slope predicts the change in $y$ for one more unit of $x$, not the reverse.
steps: The slope $17$ pairs a $1$-unit increase in $x$ with a change in $y$.
One unit of $x$ is one practice test; $y$ is measured in points.
Word it as a prediction on average, not as a cause.
problems.verify: result = 'On average, each additional practice test is associated with a predicted increase of $17$ points in score improvement.'

problems.stem: The line of best fit relating $x$, the number of weeks of training, to $\hat{y}$, the predicted number of push-ups an athlete can complete, is $\hat{y}=2.5x+18$. For what value of $x$ does this model predict $68$ push-ups?
problems.solution: Here the output is given and the input is unknown, so the prediction becomes an equation to solve rather than an expression to evaluate.
steps: Subtract: $2.5x=50$.
Divide: $x=20$ weeks.
problems.verify:
x = symbols('x')
result = solve(Rational(5,2)*x + 18 - 68, x)[0]

problems.stem: The table shows the actual number of bicycles a shop rented and the number predicted by the line of best fit on each of five days. On how many of these days does the model overpredict the number of rentals?
problems.solution: The model overpredicts exactly when predicted exceeds actual, that is when the residual is negative. Days $1$, $3$ and $5$ have residuals $-1$, $-2$ and $-1$; days $2$ and $4$ have residual $+2$.
steps: Compute residual $=$ actual $-$ predicted for each day.
Three residuals are negative, so the model overpredicts on $3$ days.

problems.stem: A biologist restocked a pond and then counted the fish each month. For the scatterplot of $x$, the number of months since restocking, and $y$, the number of fish, the line of best fit is $\hat{y}=34x+210$. Which of the following statements about this model is true?
choices: The predicted number of fish increases by $210$ each month, and the pond contained $34$ fish at restocking.
The predicted number of fish increases by $34$ each month, and the pond contained $210$ fish at restocking.
The predicted number of fish increases by $34$ each month, and the pond contained $34$ fish at restocking.
The predicted number of fish increases by $210$ each month, and the pond contained $210$ fish at restocking.
problems.solution: Two numbers, two jobs: the slope $34$ is a rate per month, and the intercept $210$ is the predicted count at $x=0$, the moment of restocking. Every wrong choice assigns at least one of them the other's job.
steps: Slope $=34$: the predicted monthly increase in fish.
Intercept $=210$: the predicted number of fish at $x=0$.
$x=0$ is the moment of restocking.
problems.verify: result = 'The predicted number of fish increases by $34$ each month, and the pond contained $210$ fish at restocking.'

problems.stem: The scatterplot shows the membership of a new club, in hundreds, over seven weeks. Which of the following best describes a model for these data?
choices: A linear model, because the points fall close to a straight line.
An exponential decay model, because the values decrease at a decreasing rate.
An exponential growth model, because the values increase at an increasing rate.
A linear model, because the values increase by a constant amount for each additional week.
problems.solution: The membership climbs by $2$, then $3$, then $5$, then $8$, then $13$, then $21$ hundred: the increases themselves are growing, so the points bend upward rather than following a straight line. That is exponential growth.
steps: Look at how much the height changes from one week to the next.
The changes get larger and larger, so the graph curves upward.
Increasing at an increasing rate is exponential growth, not linear.
problems.verify: result = 'An exponential growth model, because the values increase at an increasing rate.'

problems.stem: The scatterplot shows the number of tickets remaining for a concert on each of eight days after a sale began. Which of the following best describes the association shown?
choices: The association is negative and approximately linear.
The association is positive and approximately linear.
The association is negative and exponential, with the tickets halving each day.
There is no association between the day and the number of tickets remaining.
problems.solution: The points fall steadily from left to right along a nearly straight path, so the association is negative and approximately linear. A negative association does not mean the relationship is weak.
steps: Read the plot left to right.
The number of tickets falls as the days increase, so the association is negative.
The points lie close to a straight line, so the form is linear.
problems.verify: result = 'The association is negative and approximately linear.'

problems.stem: A candle's height was measured as it burned. For the scatterplot of $x$, the number of minutes since the candle was lit, and $y$, the height of the candle in centimeters, the line of best fit is $\hat{y}=15-0.2x$. Which of the following is the best interpretation of the number $15$ in this model?
choices: The candle's predicted height decreases by $15$ centimeters per minute.
The candle's predicted height when it was lit was $0.2$ centimeters.
The candle's predicted height when it was lit was $15$ centimeters.
The candle is predicted to burn out after $15$ minutes.
problems.solution: The number $15$ is the constant term, so it is the predicted height when $x=0$ minutes --- the instant the candle was lit. The rate at which the candle shortens is the other number, $0.2$ centimeters per minute.
steps: $x=0$ is the moment the candle was lit.
So the predicted starting height is $15$ centimeters.
problems.verify: result = "The candle's predicted height when it was lit was $15$ centimeters."

problems.stem: In a study of $30$ precincts, the line of best fit relating $x$, the number of registered voters in hundreds, to $\hat{y}$, the predicted number of ballots cast in hundreds, is $\hat{y}=0.8x+12$. How many hundreds of ballots does the model predict for a precinct with $35$ hundred registered voters?
problems.solution: Substitute and evaluate, keeping both variables in the same units (hundreds) so no conversion is needed.
steps: Substitute $x=35$.
Add: $28+12=40$ hundred ballots.
problems.verify: result = Rational(8,10)*35 + 12

problems.stem: For a group of phone customers, the line of best fit relating $x$, the number of text messages sent in a month, to $y$, that month's bill in dollars, is $\hat{y}=0.05x+30$. Which of the following is the best interpretation of the slope of this line?
choices: The predicted bill increases by $\$30$ for each additional text message.
The predicted bill increases by $\$0.05$ for each additional text message.
The predicted bill is $\$0.05$ when no text messages are sent.
For each additional dollar in the bill, $0.05$ more text messages are predicted.
problems.solution: The slope $0.05$ has units of dollars per text message, so each extra text adds a predicted $5$ cents to the bill. The $30$ is the predicted bill when no texts are sent.
steps: The slope is $0.05$.
One unit of $x$ is one text message; $y$ is in dollars.
So each additional text raises the predicted bill by $\$0.05$.
problems.verify: result = 'The predicted bill increases by $\\$0.05$ for each additional text message.'

problems.skill: Slope of a line of best fit
problems.stem: A line of best fit passes through the points $(4,30)$ and $(14,5)$. What is the slope of this line of best fit?
problems.solution: The $y$-values drop as the $x$-values rise, so the slope must come out negative; a positive answer means the subtraction was done in mismatched orders.
problems.verify: result = Rational(5-30, 14-4)

problems.stem: Which of the following situations is best modeled by an exponential function?
choices: A car's value decreases by $15\%$ of its current value each year.
A pool is drained at a constant rate of $12$ gallons per minute.
A worker earns $18$ dollars for each hour worked.
A tank gains $5$ liters of water every $2$ minutes.
problems.solution: A change of a fixed \emph{percent} of a changing amount is exponential, because the amount added or removed changes as the quantity changes. Fixed amounts per unit of time or per item are linear.
steps: Ask whether the change per unit is a fixed amount or a fixed percent.
A fixed amount per unit gives a constant difference, which is linear.
A fixed percent of the current value gives a constant ratio, which is exponential.
problems.verify: result = "A car's value decreases by $15\\%$ of its current value each year."

problems.stem: In a scatterplot with a line of best fit, one data point lies below the line. Which of the following must be true about that data point?
choices: The residual for that point is positive, and the model underpredicts the value.
The residual for that point is negative, and the model underpredicts the value.
The residual for that point is negative, and the model overpredicts the value.
The residual for that point is positive, and the model overpredicts the value.
problems.solution: Below the line means the actual value is smaller than the predicted value, so actual $-$ predicted is negative and the model guessed too high. Negative residual and over-prediction always travel together.
steps: Below the line means actual $<$ predicted.
Residual $=$ actual $-$ predicted, so the residual is negative.
A prediction that is too high is an over-prediction.
problems.verify: result = 'The residual for that point is negative, and the model overpredicts the value.'

problems.stem: The line of best fit for a data set is $\hat{y}=5.5x+30$. One data point in the set has $x=8$ and an actual $y$-value of $70$. What is the residual for that data point?
problems.solution: Predict first, then subtract in the order actual minus predicted. The negative result says the point lies below the line and the model overpredicts there.
steps: Residual $=$ actual $-$ predicted $=70-74$.
The residual is $-4$.
problems.verify: result = 70 - (Rational(11,2)*8 + 30)

problems.stem: The population of a town is modeled by $P(t)=4800(0.85)^{t}$, where $t$ is the number of years since $2015$. Which of the following is the best interpretation of this model?
choices: The population decreases by $85\%$ each year from an initial value of $4800$.
The population decreases by $15$ people each year from an initial value of $4800$.
The population increases by $15\%$ each year from an initial value of $4800$.
The population decreases by $15\%$ each year from an initial value of $4800$.
problems.solution: In $a(b)^t$, $a$ is the value at $t=0$ and $b$ is the yearly multiplier. Since $0.85=1-0.15$, the population keeps $85\%$ of itself and therefore loses $15\%$ each year, starting from $4800$ in $2015$.
steps: At $t=0$ the model gives $P=4800$, the population in $2015$.
The base $0.85$ multiplies the population each year.
Losing $15\%$ leaves $85\%$, so the decay rate is $15\%$ per year.
problems.verify: result = 'The population decreases by $15\\%$ each year from an initial value of $4800$.'

problems.stem: A researcher collected data for $x$ between $1$ and $12$ months and found the line of best fit $\hat{y}=45x+120$. She then used the model to predict $\hat{y}$ when $x=90$. Which of the following is the best reason to doubt that prediction?
choices: The slope of the line of best fit is positive, so the model cannot be used to make predictions.
A line of best fit can only be used for values of $x$ that appear exactly in the data set.
The $y$-intercept of $120$ is too large for the model to be accurate.
The value $x=90$ is far outside the range of the data used to build the model, so the pattern may not continue.
problems.solution: Extrapolation is the issue: a line of best fit only summarizes the range of $x$ that was actually observed. Beyond it the relationship may bend, level off, or stop existing, and the model has no evidence either way.
steps: Note the range of the data: $x$ from $1$ to $12$.
The prediction uses $x=90$, far outside that range.
Outside the observed range the pattern is not supported by evidence.
problems.verify: result = 'The value $x=90$ is far outside the range of the data used to build the model, so the pattern may not continue.'

problems.stem: The line of best fit for a set of data is $\hat{y}=-0.6x+45$. For what value of $x$ does this model predict a $y$-value of $15$?
problems.solution: Because the slope is negative, reaching a smaller predicted $y$ requires a larger $x$; setting up the equation avoids guessing at that direction.
steps: Divide: $x=50$.
problems.verify:
x = symbols('x')
result = solve(-Rational(6,10)*x + 45 - 15, x)[0]

problems.stem: For a scatterplot of $x$, the number of years since $1990$, and $y$, the average price of a movie ticket in dollars, the line of best fit is $\hat{y}=0.19x+4.2$. Which of the following is the best interpretation of the slope of this line?
choices: The predicted price of a ticket increased by about $19$ cents per year.
The predicted price of a ticket increased by about $19$ dollars per year.
The predicted price of a ticket increased by about $4.20$ dollars per year.
The predicted price of a ticket in $1990$ was about $19$ cents.
problems.solution: The slope is $0.19$ dollars per year, and $0.19$ dollars is $19$ cents. Reading the slope as $19$ dollars per year, or reading the intercept as the yearly change, are the two standard errors here.
steps: The slope is $0.19$, measured in dollars per year.
Convert: $\$0.19=19$ cents.
So the predicted price rose about $19$ cents per year.
problems.verify: result = 'The predicted price of a ticket increased by about $19$ cents per year.'

problems.stem: A machine purchased for $\$25000$ loses value according to the model $V(t)=25000(0.8)^{t}$, where $t$ is the number of years since purchase. What value does this model predict after $3$ years?
problems.solution: Each year the machine keeps $80\%$ of its value, so three years leave $0.8^3=0.512$ of the original. Subtracting $20\%$ three times as a fixed dollar amount would be the linear mistake.
steps: The predicted value is $\$12800$.
problems.verify: result = 25000*Rational(8,10)**3

problems.skill: Reading a scatterplot with a fitted line
problems.stem: The scatterplot shows seven data points together with a line of best fit. For how many of these data points is the residual positive?
problems.solution: A positive residual means the actual value is greater than the predicted value, so the point sits strictly above the line. Counting points above the line answers the question directly.
steps: A positive residual means the point lies above the line.
The line is $\hat{y}=2x+1$, giving predictions $3,5,7,9,11,13,15$.
The points $(1,5)$, $(3,10)$ and $(5,15)$ lie above it, so the count is $3$.

problems.stem: On one afternoon a weather station recorded the temperature every hour. For the scatterplot of $x$, the number of hours after noon, and $y$, the temperature in degrees Fahrenheit, the line of best fit is $\hat{y}=2.3x+68$. Which of the following is the best interpretation of the number $68$ in this model?
choices: The temperature increased by $68$ degrees Fahrenheit each hour.
The predicted temperature at noon was $2.3$ degrees Fahrenheit.
It took $68$ hours for the temperature to rise $2.3$ degrees Fahrenheit.
The predicted temperature at noon was $68$ degrees Fahrenheit.
problems.solution: Setting $x=0$ puts the clock at noon, so $68$ is the predicted temperature at noon. The hourly rise is the slope $2.3$; swapping the two numbers produces two of the wrong choices.
steps: $x=0$ means $0$ hours after noon, that is, noon itself.
So the model predicts $68$ degrees Fahrenheit at noon.
problems.verify: result = 'The predicted temperature at noon was $68$ degrees Fahrenheit.'

problems.stem: The table shows the number $N$ of cells in a culture $t$ hours after an experiment began. Which of the following equations best models these data?
problems.solution: The values triple each hour, so the model is exponential with base $3$, and the value at $t=0$ is $6$, so the coefficient in front is $6$. Writing $3(6)^{t}$ swaps the starting value with the growth factor.
steps: At $t=0$ the count is $6$, so the initial value is $6$.
The model is $N=6(3)^{t}$.

problems.stem: The table shows the actual number of visitors to a park and the number predicted by a line of best fit on each of four days. Which of the following correctly identifies the day on which the model overpredicts by the greatest amount?
choices: On day $3$ the model overpredicts by $9$ visitors.
On day $4$ the model overpredicts by $12$ visitors.
On day $2$ the model overpredicts by $7$ visitors.
On day $1$ the model overpredicts by $6$ visitors.
problems.solution: Over-prediction happens where predicted exceeds actual, that is, where the residual is negative. The residuals are $6$, $-7$, $9$ and $-12$, so the largest over-prediction is $12$ visitors, on day $4$. Days $1$ and $3$ are under-predictions and cannot be the answer at all.
steps: Compute residual $=$ actual $-$ predicted for each day: $6$, $-7$, $9$, $-12$.
Over-prediction corresponds to a negative residual: days $2$ and $4$.
The larger over-prediction is $12$ visitors on day $4$.
problems.verify: result = 'On day $4$ the model overpredicts by $12$ visitors.'

problems.stem: A study of high school students produced the line of best fit $\hat{y}=8.4-0.006x$, where $x$ is the number of minutes per day a student spends on social media and $\hat{y}$ is the predicted number of hours of sleep that student gets per night. Which of the following is the best interpretation of the number $-0.006$ in this model?
choices: For each additional minute per day on social media, the model predicts $8.4$ fewer hours of sleep per night.
For each additional hour of sleep per night, the model predicts $0.006$ fewer minutes per day on social media.
A student who spends no time on social media is predicted to sleep $0.006$ hours per night.
For each additional minute per day on social media, the model predicts $0.006$ fewer hours of sleep per night.
problems.solution: The slope pairs one extra minute of social media with a predicted change in sleep, and the negative sign makes it a decrease. Reversing the roles of the two variables, or reading $8.4$ as the rate, gives the trap choices.
steps: The slope is $-0.006$, in hours of sleep per minute of social media.
The negative sign makes the predicted change a decrease.
So one more minute per day predicts $0.006$ fewer hours of sleep.
problems.verify: result = 'For each additional minute per day on social media, the model predicts $0.006$ fewer hours of sleep per night.'

problems.stem: For a set of data the line of best fit is $\hat{y}=7.2x+15$. According to this model, how much greater is the predicted value of $y$ when $x=25$ than the predicted value of $y$ when $x=10$?
problems.solution: Differences of predictions depend only on the slope: the constant $15$ appears in both predictions and cancels when they are subtracted.
steps: The change in $x$ is $25-10=15$.
Each unit of $x$ changes the prediction by $7.2$.
So the difference is $7.2(15)=108$.
problems.verify: result = (Rational(72,10)*25 + 15) - (Rational(72,10)*10 + 15)

problems.stem: A linear model is fitted to a data set, and the residuals, listed in order of increasing $x$, are $6$, $2$, $-3$, $-5$, $-2$, $3$, and $8$. Which of the following conclusions is best supported by these residuals?
choices: The linear model is appropriate, because the residuals sum to a small number.
The linear model is appropriate, because every residual is less than $10$ in absolute value.
A nonlinear model would fit better, because the residuals move from positive to negative and back in a U-shaped pattern.
A nonlinear model would fit better, because every residual is positive.
problems.solution: Residuals from a good linear fit should scatter randomly around zero. Here they march from positive to negative and back, a U-shaped pattern that says the data curve and a straight line is the wrong shape --- no matter how small the residuals are.
steps: Track the signs in order: $+,+,-,-,-,+,+$.
That is a systematic U-shaped pattern, not random scatter.
A systematic pattern in the residuals means the linear form is wrong.
problems.verify: result = 'A nonlinear model would fit better, because the residuals move from positive to negative and back in a U-shaped pattern.'

problems.stem: For a data set the line of best fit is $\hat{y}=3.4x+12$. One data point in the set has $x=15$, and its residual is $-7$. What is the actual $y$-value of that data point?
problems.solution: Predict first, then apply the residual with its sign: actual $=$ predicted $+$ residual. Stopping at the prediction, $63$, answers a question the problem did not ask.
steps: Actual $=$ predicted $+$ residual $=63+(-7)$.
The actual $y$-value is $56$.
problems.verify: result = (Rational(34,10)*15 + 12) + (-7)

problems.stem: For $40$ employees at a firm, the line of best fit relating $x$, the number of years of experience, to $y$, the annual salary in thousands of dollars, is $\hat{y}=2.8x+41$. Which of the following gives the best interpretation of both the slope and the $y$-intercept of this model?
choices: Each additional year of experience is associated with a predicted increase of $\$2800$ in salary, and an employee with no experience is predicted to earn $\$41000$.
Each additional year of experience is associated with a predicted increase of $\$41000$ in salary, and an employee with no experience is predicted to earn $\$2800$.
Each additional year of experience is associated with a predicted increase of $\$2.80$ in salary, and an employee with no experience is predicted to earn $\$41$.
Each additional $\$2800$ of salary is associated with one more year of experience, and an employee earning no salary is predicted to have $41$ years of experience.
problems.solution: Both numbers are measured in thousands of dollars, so $2.8$ means $\$2800$ per year of experience and $41$ means $\$41000$ at zero years. Skipping the unit conversion, swapping the two roles, or reversing the variables produces the other three choices.
steps: Slope $2.8$ thousand dollars per year $=\$2800$ per year of experience.
Intercept $41$ thousand dollars $=\$41000$ predicted at $x=0$ years.
$x=0$ describes an employee with no experience.
problems.verify: result = 'Each additional year of experience is associated with a predicted increase of $\\$2800$ in salary, and an employee with no experience is predicted to earn $\\$41000$.'
